identity.title: LaMPlace: Learning to Optimize Cross-Stage Metrics in Macro Placement

problem.claim: Macro placement optimization should target final chip-quality metrics, including timing, rather than only metrics available during placement.

gap.claim: Existing methods mainly optimize intermediate surrogate metrics because post-placement evaluation of cross-stage metrics is computationally expensive, limiting practical online optimization and alignment with final performance.

contributions.claim: LaMPlace trains an offline predictor for cross-stage metrics and uses it to generate a pixel-level placement mask that estimates each grid location’s impact on design metrics.
The authors report improved chip quality across several key design metrics, with an average improvement of 9.6%.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present learning a mask for fast cross-stage-metric optimization during macro placement, replacing reliance on intermediate surrogate metrics.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report a 43.0% improvement in WNS on commonly used benchmarks.
The authors report a 30.4% improvement in TNS on commonly used benchmarks.
The authors report an average 9.6% improvement across several key design metrics.

narrative_sequence.summary: Machine learning is described as promising for macro placement, but existing approaches mainly optimize intermediate surrogate metrics.
LaMPlace learns an offline predictor and converts its estimates into a pixel-level mask used as a fast evaluator for placement decisions.
Experiments on commonly used benchmarks are reported to improve chip quality, particularly timing metrics WNS and TNS.

source_observation.claim: The abstract explicitly connects the optimization target, computational bottleneck, proposed proxy mechanism, and final metrics: offline prediction enables fast decisions based on cross-stage metrics.

lessons.interpretation: A strong abstract can explain a method as a direct response to a specific evaluation-cost and objective-misalignment problem.
lessons.application: Frame a proposed proxy or learned evaluator by stating which expensive downstream objective it estimates, how it enables decisions, and which final metric tests alignment.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the downstream metric is cheap to evaluate or when proxy error and calibration are central but unreported.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify benchmark identities, baselines, experimental protocol, statistical variation, or whether improvements are relative to a particular reference.
The reported manufacturing issues and metric improvements are author-reported; the abstract does not provide supporting details or verification conditions.
